name: The Q Continuum
title: The Continuum
description: An extradimensional plane inhabited by a race of near-omnipotent beings who exist outside normal space and time, able to reshape matter, halt time, and hurl starships across the galaxy at a thought, who occasionally intervene in the affairs of 'lesser' species to test or provoke them.

name: The Prophets
title: The Celestial Temple's Wormhole Aliens
description: Non-corporeal beings who exist outside linear time within the Bajoran wormhole, revered by the Bajoran people as gods and guardians who guided their civilization for millennia and chose Benjamin Sisko as their Emissary to the Bajoran people.

name: The Pah-wraiths
title: The Exiled Ones
description: Wormhole aliens cast out of the Celestial Temple by the Prophets long ago and banished to Bajor's fire caves, worshipped by a fringe of Bajorans as fallen gods and ultimately used by Gul Dukat in an attempt to unleash chaos upon the galaxy.

name: Q
title: Q
description: A mischievous, near-omnipotent member of the Q Continuum who first appears to put humanity on trial for its 'grievously savage nature,' then spends decades testing, tormenting, and occasionally aiding Jean-Luc Picard and other Starfleet officers he finds endlessly amusing.

name: James T. Kirk
title: Captain of the USS Enterprise
description: A brash, brilliant starship captain from Iowa who leads the USS Enterprise on a five-year mission of exploration, defeating the Kobayashi Maru's no-win scenario as a cadet by secretly reprogramming the test.

name: Spock
title: Science Officer of the USS Enterprise
description: The half-Vulcan, half-human science officer and first officer of the Enterprise, son of Ambassador Sarek and Amanda Grayson, whose lifelong struggle to reconcile Vulcan logic with human emotion makes him one of the Federation's most celebrated officers.

name: Leonard McCoy
title: Chief Medical Officer of the USS Enterprise
description: A cantankerous, deeply humane doctor from Georgia known as 'Bones,' whose blunt objections to Kirk's risk-taking and philosophical sparring with Spock form the emotional core of the Enterprise's command trio.

name: Montgomery Scott
title: Chief Engineer of the USS Enterprise
description: The resourceful Scottish chief engineer of the Enterprise, famed for coaxing miracles from the ship's engines under fire and for insisting he needs more time than he actually does.

name: Nyota Uhura
title: Communications Officer of the USS Enterprise
description: A gifted linguist and communications officer whose calm command of the Enterprise's communications station made her one of television's first Black women in a position of authority, a role that inspired a generation including Whoopi Goldberg and Mae Jemison.

name: Hikaru Sulu
title: Helmsman of the USS Enterprise
description: The Enterprise's skilled helmsman, an avid fencer and botanist who later commands his own starship, the USS Excelsior.

name: Pavel Chekov
title: Navigator of the USS Enterprise
description: The Enterprise's young, proudly Russian navigator, added to the bridge crew to appeal to a younger audience and known for insisting nearly every invention originated in Russia.

name: Sarek
title: Vulcan Ambassador to the Federation
description: A revered Vulcan ambassador to the United Federation of Planets, father of Spock and adoptive father of Michael Burnham, whose long diplomatic career and strained relationships with his children spanned more than a century.

name: Jean-Luc Picard
title: Captain of the USS Enterprise-D
description: A cerebral, principled French captain who commands the Enterprise-D and later the Enterprise-E, briefly assimilated by the Borg as Locutus before being rescued, who spends his career championing diplomacy, curiosity, and the dignity of every lifeform he encounters.

name: William Riker
title: First Officer of the USS Enterprise-D
description: Picard's loyal first officer, who repeatedly declines offers of his own command to remain at his captain's side before eventually taking command of the USS Titan.

name: Data
title: Operations Officer of the USS Enterprise-D
description: An android Starfleet officer created by Dr. Noonien Soong, found as the sole activation aboard the ruined Omicron Theta colony, whose lifelong quest to understand and emulate humanity places him among Starfleet's most beloved officers.

name: Worf
title: Chief of Security
description: A Klingon raised by human adoptive parents after the Khitomer Massacre, who serves as chief of security aboard the Enterprise-D and later as a Federation liaison to the Klingon Empire and strategic officer on Deep Space Nine.

name: Geordi La Forge
title: Chief Engineer of the USS Enterprise-D
description: A blind engineer who perceives the world through a VISOR interfacing directly with his brain, whose warmth and technical brilliance make him the Enterprise-D's chief engineer and Data's closest friend.

name: Deanna Troi
title: Ship's Counselor of the USS Enterprise-D
description: A half-Betazoid empath serving as the Enterprise-D's ship's counselor, whose ability to sense emotions proves invaluable in negotiations and crises throughout her decades of service.

name: Beverly Crusher
title: Chief Medical Officer of the USS Enterprise-D
description: The Enterprise-D's chief medical officer, widow of Starfleet officer Jack Crusher and mother of Wesley Crusher, whose long, complicated bond with Picard endures across decades.

name: Benjamin Sisko
title: Commander of Deep Space Nine
description: A widowed Starfleet officer who takes command of the space station Deep Space Nine after the Cardassian withdrawal from Bajor, and is recognized by the Bajoran people as the Emissary of the Prophets, a spiritual role he reluctantly grows to embrace.

name: Kira Nerys
title: First Officer of Deep Space Nine
description: A former Bajoran resistance fighter against the Cardassian Occupation who becomes Deep Space Nine's first officer, bringing fierce conviction and hard-won pragmatism to the station's command staff.

name: Odo
title: Chief of Security, Deep Space Nine
description: A shapeshifting Changeling found adrift and raised among Bajorans and Cardassians without knowledge of his origins, who serves as Deep Space Nine's stern but fair chief of security before discovering he is one of the Hundred sent out long ago by the Founders.

name: Jadzia Dax
title: Science Officer of Deep Space Nine
description: A joined Trill science officer carrying the centuries-old Dax symbiont, previously joined to the respected elder Curzon Dax, whose wit and courage make her indispensable aboard Deep Space Nine.

name: Kathryn Janeway
title: Captain of the USS Voyager
description: The determined captain of the USS Voyager, stranded 70,000 light-years from home in the Delta Quadrant after pursuing a Maquis ship, who leads her combined Starfleet and Maquis crew on a seven-year journey back to Federation space.

name: Chakotay
title: First Officer of the USS Voyager
description: A former Maquis captain who joins Voyager's crew after his own ship is destroyed, becoming Janeway's trusted first officer for the long journey home.

name: Seven of Nine
title: Former Borg Drone
description: A human woman assimilated by the Borg as a child and known as Seven of Nine, Tertiary Adjunct of Unimatrix Zero-One, severed from the Collective and rescued by Janeway, who slowly reclaims her individuality while serving as Voyager's astrometrics officer.

name: The Doctor
title: Emergency Medical Hologram
description: Voyager's Emergency Medical Hologram, activated after the ship's medical staff are killed and left to serve as its only doctor for seven years, growing far beyond his original programming into a singer, painter, and advocate for holographic rights.

name: Jonathan Archer
title: Captain of the Enterprise NX-01
description: The captain of Earth's first Warp 5 starship, Enterprise NX-01, whose voyages a century before Kirk's help lay the diplomatic groundwork for the eventual founding of the United Federation of Planets.

name: T'Pol
title: Science Officer of the Enterprise NX-01
description: A Vulcan science officer assigned to Enterprise NX-01 to observe humanity's first steps into deep space, who comes to respect and defend the young, impulsive species she was sent to monitor.

name: Michael Burnham
title: Captain of the USS Discovery
description: A human raised on Vulcan as the adopted daughter of Sarek and Amanda Grayson and foster sister of Spock, whose court-martial for mutiny at the start of the Federation-Klingon War gives way to a career that eventually carries her a thousand years into the future as captain of the USS Discovery.

name: Christopher Pike
title: Captain of the USS Enterprise
description: Kirk's predecessor as captain of the Enterprise, who glimpses his own crippling future in a Klingon time crystal on Boreth and chooses to command with open-hearted courage anyway, knowing a training accident will one day leave him gravely injured saving cadets.

name: Una Chin-Riley
title: First Officer of the USS Enterprise
description: Pike's first officer aboard the Enterprise, known to her crew as 'Number One,' a genetically augmented Illyrian who conceals her heritage for years before standing trial before a Starfleet court-martial for it.

name: The Borg
title: The Collective
description: A cybernetic hive mind spanning thousands of assimilated species across the galaxy, first encountered by the Federation when Q flings the Enterprise-D into their path, who conquer through forced assimilation and pursue the relentless goal of technological and biological 'perfection.'

name: Tribble
title: The Trouble with Tribbles
description: Small, round, purring, rapidly self-replicating furballs beloved by nearly every species except Klingons, whose explosive population growth aboard the Enterprise causes a minor crisis over a shipment of contaminated grain.

name: Gorn
title: The Reptilian Predators
description: A powerful reptilian species first encountered when Kirk is forced into single combat with a Gorn captain on a desert planet, later revealed as far more dangerous apex predators who besiege the Enterprise a century earlier under Pike's command.

name: Horta
title: The Devil in the Dark
description: A silicon-based, rock-like creature dwelling in the tunnels of the mining colony Janus VI, who kills miners destroying what they mistake for mineral nodules but are in fact her unhatched eggs, until Kirk and Spock broker peace through a mind meld.

name: Species 8472
title: Residents of Fluidic Space
description: A powerful, biologically-based species native to fluidic space, designated by the Borg as Species 8472, who wage a devastating war against the Collective after their space is invaded until Voyager helps negotiate an end to the conflict.

name: The Doomsday Machine
title: The Planet Killer
description: A colossal, ancient automated weapon built by a long-vanished civilization, which devours entire planets for fuel and cannot be stopped by conventional weapons, having already destroyed the USS Constellation and its crew before reaching the Enterprise.

name: Crystalline Entity
title: The Snowflake of Death
description: A vast, crystalline, snowflake-shaped lifeform that drifts through space consuming all biological energy from any world it touches, responsible for annihilating the Omicron Theta colony where Data was created and activated.

name: The Founders
title: Rulers of the Dominion
description: A xenophobic species of shapeshifting Changelings who dwell together in a communal Great Link in the Omarion Nebula and rule the Dominion, having learned to distrust 'solids' after centuries of persecution, and who wage the Dominion War against the Federation and its allies.

name: USS Enterprise (NCC-1701)
title: Flagship of the Federation
description: A Constitution-class starship and the first Federation vessel to bear the name Enterprise, launched on a historic five-year mission of exploration under Christopher Pike and later James T. Kirk.

name: USS Enterprise-D
title: The Galaxy-Class Flagship
description: A Galaxy-class starship built to carry entire families into deep space, commanded by Jean-Luc Picard for most of its service before its saucer section is destroyed crash-landing on Veridian III.

name: USS Discovery
title: The Spore-Drive Starship
description: A Crossfield-class Federation starship equipped with an experimental spore drive allowing near-instantaneous travel, which carries its crew a thousand years into the future to escape a threat to all sentient life.

name: USS Voyager
title: The Lost Intrepid-Class Starship
description: An Intrepid-class starship pulled 70,000 light-years into the Delta Quadrant by the entity known as the Caretaker, whose crew spends seven years finding their way back to Federation space.

name: Enterprise (NX-01)
title: Earth's First Warp 5 Starship
description: The first Earth starship capable of reaching Warp 5, launched under Jonathan Archer's command on humanity's first sustained voyages into deep space a century before Kirk's Enterprise.

name: Deep Space Nine
title: The Station at the Celestial Temple
description: A Cardassian-built space station orbiting Bajor, taken over by the Federation after the Cardassian Occupation ends and stationed beside the newly discovered Bajoran wormhole, making it a crossroads of trade, faith, and war.

name: Earth
title: Cradle of Humanity and Seat of the Federation
description: Homeworld of humanity and headquarters of both Starfleet and the United Federation of Planets, its capital San Francisco home to Starfleet Command and the Academy.

name: Vulcan
title: World of Logic
description: A hot, arid homeworld whose people follow the teachings of Surak, suppressing emotion in favor of pure logic, and a founding member of the United Federation of Planets.

name: Qo'noS
title: Homeworld of the Klingon Empire
description: The homeworld of the Klingon Empire, a warrior culture bound by rigid codes of honor, whose relationship with the Federation shifts from open war to uneasy alliance over the course of a century.

name: Romulus
title: Homeworld of the Romulan Star Empire
description: The secretive homeworld of the Romulan Star Empire, settled by Vulcans who rejected Surak's teachings, whose destruction by a supernova in 2387 despite Ambassador Spock's attempt to avert it reshapes Romulan history and sets the stage for the Picard era.

name: Bajor
title: Homeworld of the Bajoran People
description: A deeply spiritual world whose people endured a brutal decades-long Cardassian Occupation before liberation, and whose devotion to the Prophets of the Celestial Temple shapes nearly every aspect of Bajoran life.

name: The Bajoran Wormhole
title: The Celestial Temple
description: A stable wormhole discovered near Bajor connecting the Alpha and Gamma Quadrants, revered by Bajorans as the Celestial Temple and home to the Prophets, whose discovery transforms Deep Space Nine into one of the quadrant's most vital outposts.

name: Starfleet Academy
title: Training Ground of Starfleet's Officers
description: The principal training institution of Starfleet, headquartered in San Francisco on Earth, whose grueling curriculum and legendary Kobayashi Maru test have shaped generations of Starfleet officers.

name: United Federation of Planets
title: The Federation
description: An interstellar republic founded in 2161 by Earth, Vulcan, Andoria, and Tellar in the wake of the Earth-Romulan War, dedicated to peaceful exploration and cooperation among its many member worlds under the united banner of Starfleet.
